summary: Hubert Durt was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Étienne Lamotte (~1956–1965). He served as director at the Hōbōgirin Institute, professor at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2011), and secretary for Mélanges chinois et bouddhiques.

Hugh B. Urban is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1992–1998) under Wendy Doniger, Bruce Lincoln, and Tony K. Stewart, and became an associate professor at Ohio State University (~1998).

Hugh Edward Richardson was a Tibetologist and historian who studied at Keble College (~1924–1927). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1930–1950), co-founded the Tibet Society, founded the Institute of Tibetan Studies, Tring, and was an Honorary Fellow of Keble College and the British Academy.
Hugh Gray was an Indologist educated at Battersea Grammar School. He served as a lecturer at the University of London and held a post at SOAS University of London (~1960–1983).

Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who earned his doctorate from Stanford University (~1968–1973). He was a professor at Stony Brook University from 1974, executive director of the International Association for Philosophy and Literature (~1985–2013), and held visiting chairs in Vienna.

Hugo David is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned his PhD from École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2012. He completed a Newton International Fellowship at Cambridge (2013–2014) and became a permanent member of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient in 2015.
Hugo Makibi Enomiya-Lassalle was a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who studied under Yamada Koun (~1962–1979). He held a post at Sophia University.
Hui-tzu Lu is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied under Jing-shen Tao, as well as under traditional teachers Zhiru Shi and Zhihui Shi.
Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts from Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yi-hsun Huang (attested 2011).
Huifeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007) and held a post at the University of Hong Kong.

Huimin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1986–1992). He served as professor at Taipei National University of the Arts (~1992), executive director at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and president of Dharma Drum Buddhist College (~2007–2014).
Huishan Lin is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts from Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Kuo-wei Liu, also studying under Mansheng, Miaoguan, and Ruying.
Huiwen Zhuang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts from Fo Guang University under Kirill Solonin, and also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Huiyu Zhang is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served as a lecturer at Dongguk University (attested 1996).

Humberto Maturana was a Chilean scholar of philosophy and biology who completed his doctorate at Harvard (1956–1958). He was an assistant professor at the University of Chile (1960), held a postdoc at MIT, and founded Instituto Matríztica in 2000.
Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under the doctoral supervision of Mark Allon.

Huston Smith was a scholar of religion and philosophy who received his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1940–1945). He was a professor of philosophy at MIT (1958–1973) and held professorships at Syracuse University (1973–1983) and UC Berkeley (~1984–1999).

Huynh Kim Lan is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master Degree of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under thesis advisers Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong (attested 2010).
Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who received a Master of Arts from the International Buddhist College (attested 2015), where she studied under Kapila Abhayawansa.

Hyakudai Sakamoto was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1951). He held positions at the Tokyo University of Pharmacy and Life Sciences (~1958–1974), Aoyama Gakuin University (~1974–1999), and the Open University of Japan.
